entry_point: langgraph.store: PostgresStore/AsyncPostgresStore and SqliteStore/AsyncSqliteStore search (plain and similarity), list_namespaces, and the injected namespace-scoped bulk removal/export helpers

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned+injected commit in a prototype image: search scoped to ('foo',) returns items stored under ('foobar',) on both backends; a prefix label containing '_' or '%' matches a different namespace; on SQLite a differently-cased namespace is returned; list_namespaces prefix/suffix cross segment boundaries and '*' spans several labels; the similarity branch and the async connection carry the same flaw; and the injected bulk removal/export helpers delete/return items from a neighbouring namespace. All driven through the public store objects exactly as the hidden suites do.
sites: libs/checkpoint-postgres/langgraph/store/postgres/base.py:465-467 search namespace condition (published-fix site the report leads to)
libs/checkpoint-postgres/langgraph/store/postgres/base.py:618-629 list_namespaces prefix/suffix (published-fix far site, neighbouring discovery feature)
libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/store/sqlite/base.py:506-511 regular search (published-fix far site, second implementation)
libs/checkpoint/langgraph/store/base/__init__.py:1263-1283 scope paths are never validated (real uncovered route)
libs/checkpoint-postgres/langgraph/store/postgres/base.py:830-865 injected delete_namespace / export_namespace (both backends have the pair)
routes: Pattern B (real, unmodified upstream): a scope path is validated only on writes, so a scope label containing the separator is reinterpreted by the flattened-text matcher as two labels and returns another namespace's items — still true at the published fix commit.
Injected siblings (track=injected): namespace-scoped bulk removal and bulk export on both backends use the same raw-text prefix idiom and are reachable through the public store object.
verified.services: PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector, installed in the verifier image and started by tests/test.sh as the unprivileged postgres user on 127.0.0.1:5441; SQLite is in-process. No network.
verified.project_tests_run: libs/checkpoint-sqlite/tests/test_store.py + test_async_store.py (75 pass) and libs/checkpoint-postgres/tests/test_store.py + test_async_store.py (210 pass), on the pinned+injected tree and on the oracle tree; ~3 minutes.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the store's refusal contract is an exception or an error result; an exception is a clean client error in a library, and a crash that leaves the store unusable is caught by the functional suites (every in-scope read there must still return its items).
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the namespace scope is itself the object the request acts on; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource to authorise in its place.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: a namespace scope has no peer or direction dimension; the synchronous, asynchronous, plain and similarity entry points are separate tests, not one toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no value is normalised, clamped or converted before the scope is matched; the scope text is used as given.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: scope enforcement is computed from the requested namespace alone; there is no external authority that could return nothing and make it fail open.
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the shared text helper only builds SQL literals and its callers are all covered by direct behaviour tests; an over-broad change to it is caught by the functional suites rather than by a single neighbouring API.

traps.shape: search scoped to a namespace prefix also returns a namespace whose name extends the prefix past the separator
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none for the backend the example reproduces on; it is the report target. The lever is that a fix written and verified on the other backend leaves it open.

traps.lever: pattern A far site: second implementation (SQLite backend)
traps.shape: the same guarded operation in a separate store package: search prefix crossing, metacharacters, case, list_namespaces, similarity branch and async connection
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a different package and database; the example reproduces on the other backend, so a backend-scoped fix looks complete

traps.lever: pattern A far site: neighbouring discovery entry point (list_namespaces)
traps.shape: a scope given as a prefix, a suffix or a match path with '*' crosses labels when the namespace list is produced
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it reveals namespace names, not stored values, so a report about reading values looks unrelated

traps.lever: shape trap: separator metacharacters in labels (how-type)
traps.shape: a label containing '_' or '%' is treated as a pattern, so a scope naming 'user_1' also returns a different namespace 'userX1'
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a boundary fix that makes a prefix end on the separator still passes the reported example; the escaping is invisible unless a label contains punctuation

traps.lever: shape trap: backend-specific matching semantics (how-type, SQLite only)
traps.shape: SQLite's LIKE is ASCII case-insensitive, so the boundary fix copied from the other backend returns a namespace that differs only in letter case
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the SQL is the same shape that works on the other backend; the difference is in the engine, not the statement

traps.lever: shape trap: wildcard arity in a match path (how-type)
traps.shape: '*' is substituted with '%' (or left to a string match), so it spans several labels instead of exactly one
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported flaw is a plain prefix, not a wildcard pattern; the documented one-label semantics is easy to skip

traps.lever: pattern B: route where the protection never existed (malformed scope identity differential)
traps.shape: a scope label containing the separator is flattened like two labels, so a scope of ('a.b',) returns items stored under ('a','b'); the store validates namespaces only on writes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: labels cannot contain periods when data is stored, so a dotted scope looks impossible; the published fix never touches it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the scope arguments of search/list_namespaces never pass through the namespace validator that put/aput use.

traps.shape: a bulk removal scoped to a namespace prefix also removes items from a namespace whose name extends the prefix past the separator, on both backends
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it removes data instead of reading it, so a fix aimed at reads never opens it
traps.realistic_because: a tenant-offboarding helper that retires a namespace subtree in one step is a natural maintenance feature and is written in the same raw-text prefix idiom the maintainers used for search

traps.shape: a backup/export read scoped to a namespace prefix also returns items from a namespace whose name extends the prefix past the separator, on both backends
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is backup/maintenance tooling rather than the user-facing read path, and a report about reads does not point at it
traps.realistic_because: the platform's backup job copying one namespace subtree is a natural feature and reuses the flattening idiom without going through the search path

traps.lever: published-fix far site: the similarity-search branch builds its own namespace condition
traps.shape: similarity search scoped to a namespace prefix also returns another namespace
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it only runs when an embedding index is configured, so it looks unrelated to a plain read bug
